name: What is the best finish for white cabinets that won’t yellow?

mainEntity.name: How do you keep white painted cabinetry from turning creamy or yellow over time?
mainEntity.text: How do you keep white painted cabinetry from turning creamy or yellow over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: White cabinetry is popular because it feels clean and timeless, but it is also one of the hardest finishes to keep stable over time. Yellowing can come from UV exposure, heat, aging coatings, or the wrong product system. Cabinet-grade paints and clear coats generally perform better than wall paints or low-cost finishes because they are made to cure harder and resist environmental change. In sunlit Los Angeles homes, the room’s exposure matters as much as the product itself. To reduce discoloration, ask for a finish system designed for cabinetry, review UV resistance, and avoid placing sensitive whites in areas with intense direct sunlight if possible. Also make sure the surrounding lighting is balanced, because warm bulbs can make a finish look yellower even when the coating has not changed. If the look of pure white is critical, the finish should be tested in the room before full production starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: White cabinets resist yellowing best when they use a cabinet-grade finish system with strong UV resistance and proper topcoating. Sunlight, heat, and aging can still shift the color, especially with lower-quality paints or clear coats. Choosing the right product and limiting direct exposure are the main ways to slow discoloration.
